request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund Tweag by Modus Create's delivery of three Cardano core infrastructure work packages over 2026-2027: Peras v1, History Expiry, and Conformance Testing for Peras and Leios.

claims.claim: The proposal requests ₳18,263,496.00, stated as USD $4,565,874.00, to fund three Cardano core infrastructure work packages over 2026-2027.
The work packages are Peras v1, History Expiry, and Conformance Testing for Peras and Leios, and the proposer says they are interdependent parts of a single delivery pipeline.
Peras is described as enabling faster finality of about 2 minutes compared with about 12 minutes today, but Peras v1 remains undeployed on mainnet.
History Expiry is claimed to reduce SPO storage costs and address projected disk growth of about 1 GB per hour at 100-1000 TPS under increased throughput.
The budget is said to be based on an average market rate of $176 per hour for senior Cardano infrastructure engineers and a conservative ADA/USD conversion rate of 0.25 based on a 5-year average.
Tweag states it has been engaged on Cardano core infrastructure since January 2018, including consensus and ledger work, Ouroboros Genesis implementation, and Peras design contributions.
The proposal says all deliverables are open-source and publicly tracked, with supporting full proposal and work-package references on IPFS, Google Drive, and the Tweag project website.

The proposal states that a legal contract with Cardano Development Holdings will be administered by Intersect, with milestone-based disbursement, third-party assurance, IOG code review, and No Witness Labs validation.

The document states funds will be administered through Intersect treasury reserve and project-specific smart contracts using the Sundae Labs framework, with oversight committee sign-off rules and a cited validation transaction.
The proposer says unspent funds, funds tied to canceled or reduced deliverables, and funds not disbursed by the end of the delivery period will be returned to the Cardano Treasury.

summary: The document describes a large treasury request for open-source Cardano core infrastructure work with named work packages, administrative controls, and refund commitments, but many key economic and feasibility assertions are stated rather than substantiated in the anchor text.
